title: Differentiation
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Standard derivatives: xⁿ, eˣ, aˣ, ln x, log_a x?
cards.a:
d/dx(xⁿ) = n xⁿ⁻¹
d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ
d/dx(aˣ) = aˣ ln a
d/dx(ln x) = 1/x
d/dx(log_a x) = 1 / (x ln a).
cards.hint: Remember: base must be e for d/dx(ln x) = 1/x. If base is a, divide by ln a.

cards.q: Derivatives of all 6 standard trigonometric functions?
cards.a:
d/dx(sin x) = cos x
d/dx(cos x) = -sin x
d/dx(tan x) = sec² x
d/dx(cot x) = -cosec² x
d/dx(sec x) = sec x tan x
d/dx(cosec x) = -cosec x cot x.
cards.hint: Mnemonic: Every trig 'co-' function (cos, cot, cosec) has a NEGATIVE derivative!

cards.q: Derivatives of the 6 inverse trigonometric functions?
cards.a:
d/dx(sin⁻¹ x) = 1 / √(1 - x²)
d/dx(cos⁻¹ x) = -1 / √(1 - x²)
d/dx(tan⁻¹ x) = 1 / (1 + x²)
d/dx(cot⁻¹ x) = -1 / (1 + x²)
d/dx(sec⁻¹ x) = 1 / (|x| √(x² - 1))
d/dx(cosec⁻¹ x) = -1 / (|x| √(x² - 1)).
cards.hint: Again, inverse 'co-' functions carry an exact minus sign of their counterparts.

cards.q: State the Chain Rule for composite functions.
cards.a: If y = f(u) and u = g(x), then dy/dx = (dy/du) · (du/dx) = f'(g(x)) · g'(x).
cards.hint: Differentiate outer function first, keeping inside intact, then multiply by derivative of inside.

cards.q: Product Rule and Quotient Rule of differentiation?
cards.a:
Product Rule: d/dx(u v) = u (dv/dx) + v (du/dx)
Quotient Rule: d/dx(u / v) = [ v (du/dx) - u (dv/dx) ] / v².
cards.hint: Quotient Rule order is critical: denominator v times derivative of numerator minus numerator u times derivative of denominator.

cards.q: Derivative of an Inverse Function?
cards.a: dx/dy = 1 / (dy/dx), provided dy/dx ≠ 0.
cards.hint: HSC Board theorem proof favorite! (f⁻¹)'(y) = 1 / f'(x).

cards.q: When is Logarithmic Differentiation used and what is its technique?
cards.a: Used when function is in the form [f(x)]^[g(x)] or a complicated product/quotient. Take natural log of both sides: ln y = g(x) ln[f(x)], then differentiate implicitly wrt x.
cards.hint: Formula: dy/dx = y · [ g'(x) ln f(x) + g(x) · (f'(x) / f(x)) ].

cards.q: MHT-CET 5-second shortcut for implicit differentiation f(x, y) = c?
cards.a: dy/dx = - (∂f / ∂x) / (∂f / ∂y), where ∂f/∂x treats y as constant, and ∂f/∂y treats x as constant.
cards.hint: Saves 2 minutes per MCQ! Don't forget the negative sign in front.

cards.q: Super MHT-CET Shortcut: If xᵐ yⁿ = (x + y)ᵐ⁺ⁿ, what are dy/dx and d²y/dx²?
cards.a: dy/dx = y / x  ALWAYS, and d²y/dx² = 0  ALWAYS (for any powers m, n > 0).
cards.hint: Legendary Board & CET question! Independent of m and n, derivative is always y/x.

cards.q: MHT-CET Shortcut: If y = √[ f(x) + √[ f(x) + √[ f(x) + ... ∞ ] ] ], find dy/dx.
cards.hint: Write y = √(f(x) + y) ⇒ y² - y = f(x) ⇒ (2y - 1) dy/dx = f'(x).

cards.q: MHT-CET Shortcut: If y = f(x)^(f(x)^(f(x)... ∞)), find dy/dx.
cards.a: dy/dx = [ y² · f'(x) ] / [ f(x) · (1 - y ln f(x)) ].
cards.hint: Write y = [f(x)]^y ⇒ ln y = y ln f(x), then differentiate implicitly.

cards.q: MHT-CET Shortcut: If y = x + 1 / (x + 1 / (x + ... ∞)), find dy/dx.
cards.a: dy/dx = y / (2y - x).
cards.hint: Write y = x + 1/y ⇒ y² - xy - 1 = 0. Apply partial derivative shortcut.

cards.q: Parametric Differentiation: If x = f(t) and y = g(t), what is dy/dx?
cards.a: dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt), provided dx/dt ≠ 0.
cards.hint: Differentiate both parametric equations with respect to parameter t.

cards.q: BIG TRAP: How to find the second derivative d²y/dx² of parametric functions?
cards.a: d²y/dx² = [ d/dt (dy/dx) ] · (dt/dx) = [ d/dt (dy/dx) ] / (dx/dt).
cards.hint: #1 MHT-CET trap! Students always forget to divide by (dx/dt) at the end.

cards.q: Trigonometric substitution for algebraic expressions in inverse trig derivatives?
cards.a:
1. √(a² - x²) → put x = a sin θ (or a cos θ)
2. √(a² + x²) → put x = a tan θ
3. √(x² - a²) → put x = a sec θ
4. √[ (a - x) / (a + x) ] → put x = a cos 2θ (or a cos θ).
cards.hint: Transforms complicated roots into simple single trigonometric terms.

cards.q: Standard simplified form: d/dx[ tan⁻¹( (cos x - sin x) / (cos x + sin x) ) ]?
cards.a: d/dx[ tan⁻¹( tan(π/4 - x) ) ] = d/dx(π/4 - x) = -1.
cards.hint: Divide numerator and denominator by cos x inside tan⁻¹.

cards.q: Derivative of one function f(x) with respect to another function g(x)?
cards.hint: Treat g(x) as the parameter; differentiate both wrt x and take ratio.

cards.q: Derivative of |x| for x ≠ 0?
cards.hint: At x = 0, |x| is NOT differentiable (sharp corner: LHD = -1 ≠ RHD = +1).

cards.q: Differentiability implies continuity theorem?
cards.a: If a function is differentiable at x = a, it is ALWAYS continuous at x = a. However, converse is NOT true.
cards.hint: f(x) = |x| is continuous at x = 0, but not differentiable at x = 0.

cards.q: n-th derivative of (ax + b)ᵐ and e^(ax)?
cards.a:
dⁿ/dxⁿ [ e^(ax) ] = aⁿ e^(ax)
dⁿ/dxⁿ [ (ax + b)ⁿ ] = aⁿ · n!.
cards.hint: Each differentiation brings down a factor of the linear coefficient a.

cards.q: n-th derivative of sin(ax + b) and cos(ax + b)?
cards.a:
dⁿ/dxⁿ [ sin(ax + b) ] = aⁿ · sin(ax + b + nπ/2)
dⁿ/dxⁿ [ cos(ax + b) ] = aⁿ · cos(ax + b + nπ/2).
cards.hint: Each successive differentiation advances the angle phase by π/2.

cards.q: Derivative of sin⁻¹(2x / (1 + x²)) and cos⁻¹((1 - x²) / (1 + x²))?
cards.a: Both equal 2 tan⁻¹ x for |x| ≤ 1. Their derivative is 2 / (1 + x²).
cards.hint: Substitute x = tan θ. Beware of domain: outside [-1, 1], sign flips!

cards.q: Derivative of tan⁻¹( (3x - x³) / (1 - 3x²) )?
cards.a: = 3 tan⁻¹ x ⇒ Derivative = 3 / (1 + x²).
cards.hint: Substitute x = tan θ to utilize triple angle identity tan 3θ = (3 tan θ - tan³ θ)/(1 - 3 tan² θ).

cards.q: How to differentiate a 3×3 determinant whose elements are functions of x?
cards.a: Differentiate one row at a time while keeping the other two rows unchanged, and sum the 3 determinants (or row-by-row / column-by-column).
cards.hint: d/dx |Δ| = |Δ₁| + |Δ₂| + |Δ₃|, where Δᵢ has row i differentiated.

cards.q: Derivative of an Even function vs an Odd function?
cards.a:
The derivative of an EVEN function is always ODD.
The derivative of an ODD function is always EVEN.
cards.hint: Example: d/dx(cos x) = -sin x (even → odd); d/dx(sin x) = cos x (odd → even).
